title: Web framework: REST, validation and errors
description: REST controllers and routing, status codes, request validation with DTOs, response models, and global error handling in Spring Boot and FastAPI.
source: Spring MVC and Bean Validation docs; Spring Framework ProblemDetail docs; FastAPI docs (handling errors, response model); Pydantic docs; MDN HTTP status codes; Baeldung
seriesDescription: Topic-by-topic JEE-style quizzes for the backend and AI-engineering interview roadmap: integer, assertion-reason, matrix match, fill-in-the-blanks, short code writing, plus multi-correct questions. Language core, concurrency, DSA, web frameworks, data access, databases, messaging, resilience, security, testing, system design, LLM and agent engineering.

questions.prompt: Match each situation with the most appropriate HTTP status code.

left.text: Signup rejected: the e-mail already exists (unique constraint)
DELETE succeeded and there is nothing to return
Valid login, but the user may not access the admin area
Request has no or an invalid credential

questions.explanation: 201 Created (with a Location header), 409 Conflict for state conflicts such as duplicates, 204 No Content, 403 Forbidden for authenticated-but-not-allowed and 401 Unauthorized for missing or bad credentials. 422 is for well-formed but semantically invalid bodies.

questions.prompt: A Spring MVC controller takes @Valid @RequestBody CreateUserRequest. The JSON body violates a @NotBlank constraint and nothing else customises error handling. What HTTP status code does the client receive?
questions.explanation: The resolver throws MethodArgumentNotValidException, which DefaultHandlerExceptionResolver turns into 400 Bad Request. FastAPI uses 422 instead.

questions.prompt: A FastAPI route takes body UserIn with name: str = Field(min_length=2), age: int = Field(ge=18) and password: str (required). A client posts {"name": "b", "age": 10}. How many entries are in the 422 response's detail list?
questions.explanation: Pydantic collects all errors rather than stopping at the first: name too short, age below 18, and password missing. One entry each.

questions.prompt: These routes are declared in this order: @app.get("/users/{uid}") def get(uid: int) and then @app.get("/users/me") def me(). What does GET /users/me return?

options.text: 422 with an int parsing error on uid.
options.why: Routes match in declaration order, so /users/{uid} captures 'me' and int validation fails.
This would only happen if the static route was declared first.
FastAPI does not detect ambiguity; the first matching route wins.

options.text: 500 at startup because the two route patterns overlap and clash.
options.why: Declaring both is legal and causes no startup error.

questions.explanation: Declare fixed paths (/users/me) before parameterised ones (/users/{uid}). Verified by running the app.

questions.prompt: Write a Spring @RestController method for POST /users. It takes a validated CreateUserRequest body, calls service.create(req) which returns a UserResponse, and answers 201 Created with that body.
questions.explanation: ResponseEntity.created(uri).body(out) is even better because it sets the Location header. @ResponseStatus(HttpStatus.CREATED) on the method is another valid way.

questions.prompt: Write a Pydantic v2 model SignupIn with email: str and password: str (at least 8 characters, using Field). Add a field_validator on email that raises ValueError unless it contains '@' and otherwise returns it lower-cased.
questions.starter: from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, field_validator
questions.explanation: Pydantic v2 uses field_validator (v1 used validator). A ValueError in a validator becomes a 422 entry in FastAPI. Annotated types such as EmailStr (needs email-validator) are an alternative.

questions.prompt: Write a Spring global handler: a class annotated for all controllers with an @ExceptionHandler method for MethodArgumentNotValidException that returns a ProblemDetail with status 400 and the detail "Validation failed".
questions.explanation: ProblemDetail is Spring 6 / Boot 3's RFC 7807-style body (media type application/problem+json). Extending ResponseEntityExceptionHandler is another common pattern.

questions.prompt: A custom exception class OutOfStock(Exception) exists. Register a FastAPI handler so it produces HTTP 409 with JSON {"error": "out_of_stock"}.
questions.explanation: Handlers receive the request and the exception. For built-in errors you can override RequestValidationError or HTTPException handlers the same way.

questions.prompt: Judge the assertion and the reason.
questions.assertion: In Bean Validation, a String field annotated only with @NotNull accepts the empty string.
questions.reason: @NotNull checks only that the value is not null.

whys.a: Correct: "" is not null, so @NotNull passes; @NotEmpty or @NotBlank is needed to reject it.
whys.b: Wrong: R is exactly the reason.

questions.explanation: NotNull < NotEmpty < NotBlank. NotBlank also rejects whitespace-only strings and applies to CharSequence only. Also remember @Size(min=3) passes null.

questions.prompt: Judge the assertion and the reason.
questions.assertion: FastAPI answers 422 when a path parameter declared as int receives the text abc.
questions.reason: FastAPI is built on top of Starlette.

whys.a: Wrong: Starlette alone would not give 422; Pydantic validation does.
whys.b: Correct: both are true, but the 422 comes from Pydantic type validation of the declared annotation.
whys.d: Wrong: A is true; the detail has type int_parsing.

questions.explanation: FastAPI validates path, query, header and body values against type hints and returns 422 with a detail array on failure.

questions.prompt: Judge the assertion and the reason.
questions.assertion: A FastAPI route with response_model=UserOut will not leak a password field returned by the function.
questions.reason: response_model only affects the OpenAPI docs and never changes the response body.

whys.c: Correct: A is true because the return value is filtered and serialised through UserOut; R is false because filtering is real.

questions.explanation: response_model validates and filters the output, so extra fields are dropped. The same discipline in Spring is returning a DTO or record rather than the JPA entity.

questions.prompt: Judge the assertion and the reason.
questions.assertion: In Spring, a @Valid failure on a @RequestBody makes Spring throw ConstraintViolationException.
questions.reason: A @Valid failure on a @RequestBody makes Spring throw MethodArgumentNotValidException.

whys.d: Correct: body binding errors raise MethodArgumentNotValidException; ConstraintViolationException belongs to method-level validation (@Validated).

questions.explanation: Handle MethodArgumentNotValidException for bodies and ConstraintViolationException (or HandlerMethodValidationException in Spring 6.1+) for parameters.

questions.prompt: Fill in the Spring MVC binding annotations.
questions.text: Use {1} to bind a segment of the URL path, {2} to bind a query-string parameter, and {3} to deserialise the JSON request body.
questions.explanation: @RequestHeader reads headers and @ModelAttribute binds form fields. In FastAPI the equivalents are inferred from the signature: Path(), Query() and a Pydantic body parameter.

questions.prompt: Given @app.post("/users", response_model=UserOut) def mk(u: UserIn): return u, where UserIn has name (stripped and title-cased by a validator), age and password, and UserOut has only name and age. A client posts {"name": " bo ", "age": 20, "password": "x"}. What comes back?

options.why: The validator ran on input and the filter dropped password on output.

options.text: Status 201 with {"name": "bo", "age": 20, "password": "x"} echoed back to the client.
options.why: Default status is 200 and password is filtered out.

options.text: Status 422 because the returned object is not a UserOut.
options.why: FastAPI converts the returned object via the response model.
The input validator already cleaned the name before the handler ran.

questions.explanation: Verified by running it. POST gives 200 unless status_code=201 is declared.

questions.prompt: Select all that apply: which of these are default FastAPI/Starlette behaviours?

options.text: A missing required query parameter gives 422.
options.why: The query parameter is validated and a missing value is a validation error.
No route matches, so Starlette returns Not Found.

options.text: A POST to a path that only has GET gives 405.
options.why: The path matches but the method does not, so Method Not Allowed.
The default handler serialises detail as JSON.

options.text: An unhandled ValueError in the route gives 400.
options.why: Unhandled exceptions become a 500 Internal Server Error.

options.text: A validation error gives 400 with a plain text body.
options.why: FastAPI returns 422 with a JSON detail list.

questions.explanation: Verified by running the app. Customise with exception_handler for HTTPException, RequestValidationError or your own types.
